generation.domain: nonsingular real linear system; no exchanges; integer entries

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-4y+4z&=-4 \\ -2x+7y-z&=1 \\ 2x-5y+z&=-1\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -4 & 4 & -4 \\ -2 & 7 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -5 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -2 \\ -2 & 7 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -5 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -3 \\ 2 & -5 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -3 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=\frac{1}{3}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y+2z&=-2 \\ y+z&=-1 \\ z&=-1\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=-1 \\ y&=-1-(1)(-1)=0 \\ x&=-2-(-2)(0)-(2)(-1)=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 0,0,-1\rangle$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & -6 & -6 & 12 \\ -2 & -2 & 0 & 10 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & -6 & -6 & 12 \\ -2 & -2 & 0 & 10 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -4 \\ -2 & -2 & 0 & 10 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=\frac{1}{2}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y+2z&=-4 \\ y+2z&=1 \\ z&=2\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=2 \\ y&=1-(2)(2)=-3 \\ x&=-4-(2)(-3)-(2)(2)=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle -2,-3,2\rangle$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & -3 & -6 & 9 \\ 1 & 3 & 6 & -5 \\ -2 & -4 & -11 & 14\end{array}\right].

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 1 & 3 & 6 & -5 \\ -2 & -4 & -11 & 14\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & -2 \\ -2 & -4 & -11 & 14\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & -7 & 8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=\frac{1}{2}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -2 & -7 & 8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y+2z&=-3 \\ y+2z&=-1 \\ z&=-2\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=-2 \\ y&=-1-(2)(-2)=3 \\ x&=-3-(1)(3)-(2)(-2)=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle -2,3,-2\rangle$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -2 & 0 & 8 \\ 2 & -4 & 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & -2 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & -4 & 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & -2 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & -6 \\ -1 & 3 & -2 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & -6 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{2}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y&=4 \\ y&=3 \\ z&=0\end{aligned}\right..

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=0 \\ y&=3-(0)(0)=3 \\ x&=4-(-1)(3)-(0)(0)=7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 7,3,0\rangle$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2x+2y-4z&=0 \\ x+y&=0 \\ -x+3y-z&=9\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & 2 & -4 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -1 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -1 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -1 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=\frac{1}{2}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=\frac{1}{3}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y+2z&=0 \\ y-z&=0 \\ z&=3\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=3 \\ y&=0-(-1)(3)=3 \\ x&=0-(-1)(3)-(2)(3)=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle -3,3,3\rangle$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-3x+6z&=0 \\ x-3y-2z&=3 \\ -x-y-z&=1\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2z&=0 \\ y&=-1 \\ z&=0\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=0 \\ y&=-1-(0)(0)=-1 \\ x&=0-(0)(-1)-(-2)(0)=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 0,-1,0\rangle$.

question.:question/problem:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x+3y+3z&=3 \\ 2x+4z&=0 \\ -2x-3y-4z&=-9\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & 3 & 3 & 3 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ -2 & -3 & -4 & -9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ -2 & -3 & -4 & -9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 & -2 \\ -2 & -3 & -4 & -9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -7\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{2}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -7\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & -6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y+z&=1 \\ y-z&=1 \\ z&=2\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=2 \\ y&=1-(-1)(2)=3 \\ x&=1-(1)(3)-(1)(2)=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle -4,3,2\rangle$.

M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & 0 & 6 & 9 \\ -2 & -3 & -7 & 9 \\ -1 & 2 & -2 & -5\end{array}\right].

$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 & 15 \\ -1 & 2 & -2 & -5\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 & 15 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 8\end{array}\right].

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -4\end{array}\right].
